status.label: Out
status.shortComment: The Eagles have ruled Hurts out for Sunday's game against the Panthers after a follow-up ultrasound performed on his calf Wednesday revealed movement in a small blood clot, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
status.longComment: According to a statement from the team, Hurts requested treatment for his calf following practice Oct. 8, a few days after he had been cleated in the leg during the team's Week 4 loss to the Rams. He underwent an initial ultrasound Saturday following the Eagles' flight to London, with imaging revealing the superficial blood clot. After the results of the ultrasound were reviewed, doctors determined that Hurts could safely play in the Eagles' eventual 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. However, after practicing fully Wednesday to kick off Week 6 prep, the quarterback was sent in for a follow-up ultrasound, which showed movement in the blood clot. As a result, the Eagles have elected to hold Hurts out of action for at least one game, with backup Tanner McKee now primed to start against the Panthers. Since the Eagles are still in the process of determining the appropriate course of treatment for Hurts, his status beyond Week 6 is uncertain at the moment.

status.label: Out
status.shortComment: Barkley (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
status.longComment: Barkley hasn't practiced the past two weeks and now appears likely to miss a second game. The Eagles will be short-handed, to say the least, with QB Jalen Hurts (blood clot) now joining the long list of starters to miss time this season. If Barkley is indeed inactive, Dameon Pierce will be the favorite to start at running back for Philadelphia.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: The Eagles placed Shipley (foot) on injured reserve Friday.
status.longComment: After being diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia earlier this week, Shipley was slated for a multi-week absence, and he now will miss at least the next four games while on IR. He'll join Tank Bigsby (abdomen) on the list, and with Saquon Barkley currently tending to a lingering hamstring injury, the Eagles have just two healthy RBs (Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele) on the active roster. Shipley's next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 22 against the Steelers.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: Stowers (quadriceps) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
status.longComment: The rookie second-rounder was placed on injured reserve prior to Week 1 due to a quadriceps injury. He opened Week 6 prep with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday, but he won't be eligible to make his NFL debut unless he's activated from IR on Saturday.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: Dickerson (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against Carolina.
status.longComment: Dickerson was cleared to return to practice Wednesday and was limited in all three sessions of Week 6 prep. He will need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be eligible to play Sunday.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Kendall (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
status.longComment: Kendall ended the week with back-to-back limited practices to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's contest. Jake Majors would start at center if Kendall is not cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a knee injury.

status.label: Out
status.shortComment: Hunt (ankle/knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against Carolina.
status.longComment: Hunt was held out of practice all week due to ankle and knee injuries, which he picked up during the Eagles' Week 5 loss to the Jaguars in London. Hist next chance to play is Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26, and in Hunt's absence, Arnold Ebiketie is in line for more rotational snaps behind Nolan Smith and Jonathan Greenard.

status.label: Doubtful
status.shortComment: Epenesa (back) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
status.longComment: Epenesa was unable to practice Thursday or Friday due to a back injury, and it looks like he'll miss his first game of the season as a result. With Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) sidelined, Arnold Ebiketie would be the lone rotational option at edge rusher if Epenesa is in fact ruled out.

status.label: Out
status.shortComment: Carter (abdomen) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
status.longComment: Carter suffered an abdominal injury in Week 5 against the Jaguars, and the injury is severe enough for him to miss all three practices during Week 6 prep. Kenny Moore will serve as the top depth option at safety behind Marcus Epps and Andrew Mukuba due to the absence of Carter, whose next chance to play is Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26.
